b2-36-01.title: Communicative Challenge: It Was Yesterday
b2-36-01.scenario: In the night train, the writer asks you, a fellow passenger, when you read the new book.
b2-36-01.prompt: Tell the writer that it was yesterday, not today, that you read the book.
cues: Say when you read the book
Stress that it was yesterday, not another day
b2-36-01.target: TEGNAP olvastam el a könyvet, nem ma.
b2-36-01.english: It was yesterday that I read the book, not today.
b2-36-01.canDo: I can put the focus word before the verb and move the preverb behind it

b2-36-02.title: Communicative Challenge: A Shorter Sentence
b2-36-02.scenario: In the compartment, Esti Kornél shows you the writer's long sentence about the resolution that the committee adopted and asks how to make it shorter.
b2-36-02.prompt: Tell Esti Kornél a shorter way to say it, with the committee and the resolution.
b2-36-02.target: A bizottság által elfogadott határozat kötelező.
b2-36-02.english: The resolution adopted by the committee is binding.
b2-36-02.canDo: I can condense a relative clause into a participial phrase before the noun, with által

b2-36-03.title: Communicative Challenge: A Polite Objection
b2-36-03.scenario: The writer shows you his plan on the train, and Esti Kornél asks you how to criticise it politely.
b2-36-03.prompt: Tell the writer politely that the plan should be thought over again, but that the idea is good.
cues: Say what is good about the plan
b2-36-03.target: Indokolt volna még egyszer átgondolni a tervet; mindazonáltal az ötlet jó.
b2-36-03.english: It would be justified to think the plan over once more; nevertheless the idea is good.
b2-36-03.canDo: I can soften a criticism with célszerű lenne and indokolt volna

b2-36-04.title: Communicative Challenge: An Old Word
b2-36-04.scenario: The writer found an old word in a novel and asks you what to do when he does not know a word.
b2-36-04.prompt: Tell the writer how to understand an unknown word in a classic text.
b2-36-04.target: Ha nem ismersz egy szót, a szövegkörnyezetből megértheted, és olvass tovább.
b2-36-04.english: If you do not know a word, you can understand it from the context, and read on.
b2-36-04.canDo: I can read a short literary text and use the context to understand an old word

b2-36-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Last Sentence
b2-36-05.scenario: Esti Kornél asks you to say the closing sentence of a short speech about one's own voice.
b2-36-05.prompt: Close the speech for Esti Kornél.
cues: Start with the word for finally
b2-36-05.target: Végül azt szeretném mondani, hogy mindenkinek meg kell találnia a saját hangját.
b2-36-05.english: Finally I would like to say that everybody must find their own voice.
b2-36-05.canDo: I can structure a short speech with an opening, an argument and a closing with végül

b2-36-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Good Speech
b2-36-consolidation.scenario: On the train, the writer asks you what makes a speech good.
b2-36-consolidation.prompt: Tell the writer two things that make a speech good.
b2-36-consolidation.target: Egyrészt a jó érvek számítanak, másrészt a természetes előadásmód.
b2-36-consolidation.english: On the one hand good arguments count, on the other hand a natural delivery style.
b2-36-consolidation.canDo: I can use focus, participial phrases and softening formulas in one text
